doc.brief: Shows a "light switch" that has two states: on or off.
doc.md:
Shows a "light switch" that has two states: on or off.

The user can control which state should be active by clicking the
empty area, or by dragging the slider.

`GtkSwitch` can also express situations where the underlying state changes
with a delay. In this case, the slider position indicates the user's recent
change (represented by the [`Switch:active`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Switch#property:active) property), while the
trough color indicates the present underlying state (represented by the
[`Switch:state`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Switch#property:state) property).

See [`Switch::state-set`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Switch#event:state-set) for details.

# Shortcuts and Gestures

`GtkSwitch` supports pan and drag gestures to move the slider.

# CSS nodes

```
switch
├── image
├── image
╰── slider
```

`GtkSwitch` has four css nodes, the main node with the name switch and
subnodes for the slider and the on and off images. Neither of them is
using any style classes.

# Accessibility

`GtkSwitch` uses the [`AccessibleRole.switch`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AccessibleRole#value:switch) role.

get_active.brief: Gets whether the `GtkSwitch` is in its “on” or “off” state.
get_active.md: Gets whether the `GtkSwitch` is in its “on” or “off” state.

get_state.brief: Gets the underlying state of the `GtkSwitch`.
get_state.md: Gets the underlying state of the `GtkSwitch`.

set_active.brief: Changes the state of `self` to the desired one.
set_active.md: Changes the state of `self` to the desired one.

set_state.brief: Sets the underlying state of the `GtkSwitch`.
set_state.md:
Sets the underlying state of the `GtkSwitch`.

This function is typically called from a [`Switch::state-set`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Switch#event:state-set)
signal handler in order to set up delayed state changes.

See [`Switch::state-set`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Switch#event:state-set) for details.

active.brief: Whether the `GtkSwitch` widget is in its on or off state.
active.md: Whether the `GtkSwitch` widget is in its on or off state.

state.brief: The backend state that is controlled by the switch.
state.md:
The backend state that is controlled by the switch.

Applications should usually set the [`Switch:active`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Switch#property:active) property,
except when indicating a change to the backend state which occurs
separately from the user's interaction.

See [`Switch::state-set`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Switch#event:state-set) for details.

activate.md:
Emitted to animate the switch.

Applications should never connect to this signal,
but use the [`Switch:active`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Switch#property:active) property.

state-set.brief: Emitted to change the underlying state.
state-set.md:
Emitted to change the underlying state.

The ::state-set signal is emitted when the user changes the switch
position. The default handler calls [`Switch.set_state()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Switch#method:set_state) with the
value of `state`.

To implement delayed state change, applications can connect to this
signal, initiate the change of the underlying state, and call
[`Switch.set_state()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Switch#method:set_state) when the underlying state change is
complete. The signal handler should return `TRUE` to prevent the
default handler from running.
